messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: cont-batch runtime p99 latency spike in us-west-2. Severity=SEV3. Detect: p99 > 2.5s over 5m. error-rate unchanged.

Kai: ack, I'm on it. opening cont-batch dashboards now https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/contbatch-latency?orgId=1

Mira: I see streaming stalls on traces. p95 ~ 300ms, p99 ~ 3.1s in the last 5m window.

Kai: initial correlation: only continuous-batching path impacted. non-streaming gen looks fine. suspect mixed sequence lengths forming oversized batches -> padding amplification + KV-cache thrash -> streaming stall tail.

Seb: any recent deploys or model imports? @deploy-bot any infra events?

deploy-bot: No deploys in last 60m. Autoscaler: scaled up usw2-gpu-pool +2 nodes at 2364509800; scale completed.

Nora: snippet from batcher logs around spike:
```
2026-03-14T09:02:11Z batcher.INFO batch_formed id=abc123 size=64 median_seqlen=120 max_seqlen=1024
2026-03-14T09:02:11Z runtime.WARN kvcache.evictions rate=0.45 host=gpu-112
2026-03-14T09:02:12Z scheduler.DEBUG preempt_check delayed=72ms preempted=0
2026-03-14T09:02:13Z stream.ERROR stall_detected request=xyz pid=3344 tail_ms=2840
```

Mira: that max_seqlen=1024 with batch size 64 explains the amplification. lots of padding + KV churn.

Kai: immediate mitigations I propose:
- lower cont-batch max_batch_size to 8 (temp)
- enable sequence-length segregation toggling seqseg.enabled=true
- shift 20% streaming traffic to fallback gen-stream-safe-v1 (CPU) to reduce risk for customers while we stabilize

Seb: +1 on lowering batch size. Nora, can seqseg be flipped via config or requires deploy?

Nora: seqseg is a runtime feature-flag we can flip from console; low risk but throughput may drop for a bit.

Kai: applying batch size change now:
```
redwoodctl runtime update-config cont-batch --set max_batch_size=8 --env usw2
```
(applied at 2364509850)

Mira: first 30s after change: p95 ~ 290ms, p99 down to ~1.2s trending lower. :thumbsup:

Seb: Nora please set traffic split for fallback and open a routing ticket so CS knows about potential cost impact.

Nora: executing traffic split at 2364509895:
```
redwoodctl traffic-split set cont-stream 0.2=gen-stream-safe-v1,0.8=cont-default --env usw2
```
ops-observer: FYI fallback increases token cost; cost-alerts updated.

Mira: ready to enable seqseg? short/long bucketing should prevent long-seq requests from mixing with short ones.

Kai: go ahead Nora.

Nora: flipping seqseg.enabled=true at 2364509908. config applied. watching KV metrics.

Mira: p99 now ~ 650ms and stable. KV eviction rate back to baseline. streaming stalls largely gone.

Kai: root cause summary for handoff: cont-batcher built large mixed-length batches (e.g., median 120 + one 1024) causing padding amplification, KV cache evictions, and streaming tail latency >2.5s. Contributing: a sudden influx of long-seq requests coincident with max_batch_size still at 64.

Mitigations applied:
- max_batch_size reduced to 8 (temporary)
- sequence-length segregation enabled (short/long buckets)
- 20% streaming traffic routed to CPU fallback variant
- closely monitored p95/p99 and KV evictions until stabilization

Seb: customer impact note: multiple high-throughput customers experienced p99 >2s for approximately 8 minutes; no errors returned, only latency. I'll compile org IDs and exact windows for CS.

Nora: followups/tasks:
- manual revert of max_batch_size after safe observation window (owner: Kai)
- create cross-zone canary for seqseg (owner: Mira)
- add alert to detect mixed-seqlen batch amplification earlier (owner: Seb)
- run batch-sizing simulation with current traffic mix to determine safer defaults (owner: eng-ml)

Kai: handing off to next oncall Jordan. Handoff summary:
- incident: cont-batch tail latency spike from mixed-seqlen batches -> mitigated
- actions: lowered batch size, enabled seqseg, 20% to fallback
- current state: p99 ~ 600ms, KV evictions normal, streaming stalls mitigated; monitor p95/p99 for 30m
- runbook: https://confluence.internal/r/contbatch-runbook

Jordan: acked. I'll watch for next 30m and will page if p99 exceeds 1.5s. post-incident: investigate region defaults for max_batch_size.

Kai: thanks all, marking incident mitigated and leaving channel open for any anomalies. :white_check_mark:
